read_extent: All four original Parlamentwatch pages read; the full current official texts of AbgG §§ 45, 47 and 52 read through the web tool. No 2021 enactment chain or identified 2026 draft independently verified.
verdict: Do not promote an established options-disclosure error; retain only unresolved wording/scope question if useful.
reason: The document concerns private wealth and ownership or portfolio interests. Privately acquired options are a concrete natural reading, whereas § 45(3) treats options granted as consideration for work as income. That separate income rule does not definitively refute the private-wealth premise. The unqualified only wording permits a broader reading, but meaning remains uncertain.
primary_rules: Section 45(2) no. 6 uses a company-holding threshold above 5 percent and provides an indirect-holding rule.
Section 45(3) treats remuneration options and comparable instruments as income, with valuation and reporting conditions.

Section 47 publishes reportable information and describes unquantifiable rights. Section 52 delegates implementing rules. The tax agent clarified that the earlier 52 reference was a web line number, rather than a section number.
scope_gate: The author requests reform of the Abgeordnetengesetz and ministerial transparency, but an exact addressed federal draft or version remains unidentified. A registered reform interest does not itself establish which bill is addressed.
limits: No judgment on specific MPs’ actual disclosures, stock-trading conflicts, US deadlines or constitutional merits. No additional original quotations added.
